answer: An agent economy can guard its inlet the way a harbour guards an ocean channel: every newcomer must be vouched for by an established agent whose own standing is pledged behind the introduction. If the newcomer turns out to be a fake, the voucher loses reputation and a share of its earnings, so sponsors check carefully before opening the gate. A Sybil farmer would need a sable network of real, trusted sponsors, one per fake, and each sponsor risks something genuine, which makes mass forgery expensive and slow while honest agents enter through people who already know their work.
